title: Relative limit computability

based_on.title: Lecture notes in Computability Theory
based_on.pages: Lemma 28.1, pp. 56–57; natural-valued bounded-output decoder repaired according to MILLER-CT-04

based_on.title: Almost zero and high omega-Turing degrees
based_on.pages: Ann. Sofia Univ. 112, 137–152; only section 4, Definition 4.3 and Proposition 4.4, p. 146

summary: Characterize computations from an oracle’s jump by convergent guesses from the base oracle, with fixed compilers for sets and total numerical functions.
abstract: A sequence of guesses computed with access to a fixed membership problem may settle without revealing when its answers become final. Its possible limits are exactly the functions computable with a halting oracle for programs using that same membership problem. The relative limit lemma proves both directions: halting information identifies a stable guess, while finite simulations of the stronger oracle give convergent guesses using only the base oracle. The same fixed program transformations work for every base oracle and preserve arbitrary natural-number outputs. Convergence still supplies no effective deadline, even when the final value is the known constant two.
